reasons: narrow: Unconditional downward closure is false because lowering a budget can make the model infeasible or the positive-\(H\) target empty. For an explicit witness, take one cell with all units selected, complier mass \(0.4\), defier mass \(0.6\), and no same-treatment types. Its observed first stage is \(-0.2\), so the pair \((\delta_D,\delta_S)=(0,0)\) is infeasible, while at \((0.6,0)\) the target exists and belongs to \(\mathcal R_0\). The valid conclusion is downward closure relative to pairs at which the target exists; the finite-chart boundary clause also requires the rational-input premise of the theorem it invokes.

narrow: The geometric and linear-program claims hold for arbitrary real inputs, but an LP has rational data only when \(q\), \(\delta_D\), and \(\delta_S\) are rational. The proposed statement adds exactly that necessary qualification, restricts branch endpoints to branches with positive denominator, and records that infeasible normalized programs certify the other branches.

narrow: The current equality is ill typed: its left side is projected onto \((d,h,n)\), whereas \(Q_o\) contains the full reduced array. The corrected statement applies the same projection to the union. It also makes the numerical rationality claim conditional on rational observed masses and budgets; arbitrary real probability inputs need not define a rational polytope.

verdict.note: Accepted after independent math adjudication: projection types aligned, rationality properly conditioned, positive-H branch scope explicit, and breakdown closure correctly restricted to the target-existence domain. No crux assumption or kernel degradation.
